items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: I spotted Steve Jordan in the audience standing on the floor. And I said, “Steve, come on up and play.”

ctx.x: Well the shows that we did with Stuff, you know backing up Joe Cocker. Somebody just posted them on FaceBook recently. You know we did “Feelin’ All Right” with Joe Cocker and John Belushi comes out and surprises him, imitating Joe Cocker, which broke Joe Cocker’s heart. I mean it was a total surprise to him. And then we do another tune, “Foots” in the second half of the show, which is really the band at its finest. You know everybody’s playing great and everybody’s alive. There’s another show with Bryan Ferry…

and he couldn’t get back into the building. I don’t know if he forgot his ID or somebody wouldn’t let him back into the building. So it’s 11:59 or something and the band is about to go on and Bryan Ferry said, “I need that conga part, I need the percussion part.” And Sammy had a set-up of five drums, five congas. And I’d been digging him all week. So he said, “Can you play the conga part?” And I said uhhh sure. So I played this conga part and literally ten seconds before air I spotted Steve Jordan in the audience…

Let me talk about — I went to your website that was just for your visual art and I scrolled — it said sketch books. And I scrolled down and I said you have almost as many sketch books as you do LP credits. It’s a great idea. And it made me think — you probably are aware that both Milt Hinton and Joe Wilder carried a camera wherever they went. And they have just these kinds of pictures that no one else would get. And I was wondering, with all the — this question I have found the answer to — how did you find time…
